remaining_conditions: A bounded 32-field native C/Rust trace covers the selected initial compiler-TLS roots and identity, count-zero image, positive regular-slot reset, and local cached-root/reference pair. It does not bind the same-TLD terminal sequence in src/init.c:mi_thread_theaps_done (377-421): default/cached reset, shared-list detach, and final teardown. Rust's static/default attachment and dynamic/cached attachment use separate TLD images, so compiler TLS remains partial.
The later process/thread lifecycle, page-bearing TLS attachment, and public runtime integration stay explicitly outside this M1 component.

exclusions.reason: The whole include/mimalloc/types.h and include/mimalloc/internal.h units remain partial. The complete represented-layout component covers only mi_memkind_t, the complete mi_memid_t representation, selected page field types, the default-release mi_page_t image through memid, mi_page_kind_t, mi_page_queue_t, and the named pure memory-ID constructors. Heap/Theap/subprocess/TLD/arena/statistics representations and generic allocator algorithms remain separate nonclaims.

The M1 vector proves the mi_memid_t.mem.arena field representation only. mi_memid_arena, source arena-ID construction, the arena branch of _mi_memid_size, MI_MEM_EXTERNAL ownership transition, mi_arena_t, and mi_arena_pages_t require a live arena or externally managed mapping. Their pointer validity, slice bounds, slice-size policy, and ownership lifecycle belong to M2 arena management and are not implied by M1 layout parity.

The represented-layout component is restricted to the selected MI_PAGE_META_IS_ALIGNED=1, MI_ENCODE_FREELIST=0, MI_PADDING=0 release image. mi_page_t::keys and mi_padding_t are absent from that image; secure, encoded-freelist, padding, and other nondefault layout modes require their own option/mode contract and do not silently count as M1 coverage.

mi_heap_t, mi_theap_t, mi_subproc_t, and mi_tld_t require later ownership, lock, thread, and page lifecycle acceptance. Existing prefix records remain bounded supporting evidence and are not a full C-layout or lifecycle claim in M1.
mi_stats_t and all statistic-bearing type tails are M7 statistics work. Their absence is not hidden by the M1 default-page metadata layout proof.

_mi_prim_reuse has no Rust raw primitive, and _mi_prim_alloc_huge_os_pages plus its huge-page VM boundary are M2 VM-substrate work. The selected normal mapping witness does not claim either declaration.
mi_process_info_t and _mi_prim_process_info are the M7 statistics surface. Rust ProcessUsage is available for later callers but is not M1 raw-primitive source-map evidence.

_mi_prim_getenv and _mi_prim_out_stderr belong to the M7 options/environment/diagnostics surface. This includes the _mi_warning_message reached by src/random.c when normal entropy fails. The selected primitive paths do not supply option parsing, environment policy, or diagnostic ownership.

_mi_prim_thread_init_auto_done, _mi_prim_thread_done_auto_done, and _mi_prim_thread_associate_default_theap require the general automatic pthread/TLS lifecycle that M5 has not closed. The exact false _mi_prim_thread_is_in_threadpool observation is separately represented.
src/prim/prim.c constructor/destructor calls to _mi_auto_process_init and _mi_auto_process_done are automatic process lifecycle work, not evidence that the generic primitive unit is ported.

src/prim/prim.c _mi_is_redirected, _mi_allocator_init, and _mi_allocator_done are allocator redirection and libc integration callbacks. The Linux raw primitive leaves do not represent that M8 boundary.

The selected normal map witness excludes unix_mmap address hints, overmap alignment, large/huge allocation routes, NUMA mbind placement, and source os.c ownership/range wrappers. Those VM-substrate routes remain M2 work.
The Unix THP option/prctl mutation, advice and secure/debug policy branches, and optional PR_SET_VMA anonymous-name diagnostic route remain M7 options/modes/diagnostics work.

The C libc fallback wrappers, clock() fallback, and getrandom ENOSYS /dev/urandom fallback are not M1 evidence: the Linux 5.10 profile uses direct crabc-core primitives and does not add a portability layer.

The selected random-image component proves the state-machine behavior of _mi_random_reinit_if_weak. Its automatic-process-initialization call site in src/init.c, including publication and lifecycle ordering, remains M5 lifecycle work and is not implied by the direct state witness.

The bounded 32-field compiler-TLS C/Rust trace proves only selected initial roots/identity, count-sensitive regular reset, and a controlled cached-root/reference pair. It does not prove src/init.c:mi_thread_theaps_done same-TLD terminal default/cached reset, shared-list detach, general cached-root switching, process/thread teardown, page-bearing attachment, or public allocator/runtime integration.
No selected M1 check is a public C allocator API, libc backend-selection, shadow-route, performance, or promotion proof.

milestone.completion_rule: M1 is complete only after every named component is changed to complete, each has no remaining condition, every required source-map status remains true, every focused check passes, and every required layout key matches in one current-commit report. Deferred exclusions remain nonclaims and do not silently count as M1 coverage.
